notes.title: Version 1.2.1
notes.content:
We've updated Dudelings with a series of features and fixes that should improve the gameplay experience! We're super stoked for this new client release as it's addressed a few long-standing issues and we're excited for your feedback.

You'll find our changelog below. If you encounter an issue, sound off in the comments or join our Revolt server.

Updates

    Reorganized game assets to simplify the process of exporting them into the FOSS build of the game
    Made some upgrades to the game’s assets to reduce overall download/disk usage size
    Backported some features/assets of the Android build to the main branch
        
            This included re-encoding the video files in the how to play and launch movie to lower bitrates
            Removing the video file that played in the background of the Main Menu and replacing it with static images that were animated in Godot
            Backported the custom virtual gamepad in the Android port to the main branch
        
    
    Added a link to our new Revolt server on the Main Menu
    Changed all links & references to our new canonical domain name: heavyelement.com
    Made some changes to the underlying code to unify the demo and retail codebase as much as possible
        
            The demo features one map, one game mode, and some customization features disabled. It should be on Steam soon!
        
    

Bug fixes

    Fixed instances where game would randomly fail to launch on Intel graphics under Linux operating systems
    Fixed a glitch where the ball could get stuck between the left- or right-most Dudeling and get placed out of bounds
    Fixed an issue with unlocking “Destination” map where criteria was met, but the map didn’t unlock until the game was restarted
    Fixed a visual glitch where labels for CheckButtons would disappear when in a hover state (thanks moocow1452)
    Fixed an issue where requests to the news endpoint failed silently
    Improved error handling for new news items on the Main Menu and in the What’s New submenu


Also, if you're a coder, we've got good news! We've launched the official Dudelings FOSS project on GitHub. This build was actually produced using the first release of our free and open source codebase. If you're interested in helping out, let us know!

Dudelings Demo
Finally, we've got excellent news! We've produced a demo version of Dudelings! Our goal is to get the game in front of folks, allow them to give it a try, and make an informed decision on if this game is worth $5. (We think it is).

The demo is available for Linux and Windows, so give that a shot.

The other thing about the demo is that it gives a free entrypoint into the open source version of the game. The assets are not licensed under the GPL, so if you want to get into development and you don't own a copy, you can download and extract the demo's assets for use with Dudelings FOSS!

notes.title: Dudelings: 2nd Base is now live!
notes.content:
Dudelings: Arcade Sportsball just received its first major update, codenamed "2nd Base," featuring a massive collection of features, fixes, and improvements to help you get your sport on!
So what's new?

Where do we even start?
Presentation
The first thing you might've noticed is the brand new CRT filter! When designing the art for the game, we had always imagined it as a Super Nintendo title. This filter lends a bit more authenticity to the design (in that kind of simulacra way). But if a CRT Filter isn't your style, you can turn it off in Settings → CRT Filter.

Then, we've added a whole bunch of new jerseys designs to the game. Jerseys have always been purely cosmetic (meaning they have no impact on the gameplay), so we decided to move them to the Settings menu. Your jersey selection will persist across game sessions and you can even change them mid-match!

Announcers
2nd Base features the voice talent of some familiar voices. YouTube sensations "FanTheDeck" and "NerdNest" have stepped up to fill the Announcer role! Select either announcer pack in Settings → Announcer Voice and enjoy the dulcet narration of some of your favorite YouTubers.

Thanks again to FanTheDeck and NerdNest for joining the Dudelings cast!

New Game Mode
2nd Base introduces a new (and exceptionally fun) game mode that we're calling "Pins." The play field is littered with a symmetrical series of pins: six for each team. Hit the ball into your opponent's pins to knock 'em down. Once all six of their pins are down, you earn a point and their pins are reset. But watch out, because yours won't reset until they score a point on you!

New Rules
Dudelings has always had the option to customize your match rules. But 2nd Base introduces a brand new and exciting victory condition: Timed Matches. Don't worry, the traditional way to play Dudelings—with a fixed Match Point—is still available. However, Timed Matches bring a whole new frenzy to the game.

And if there's a tie when the time's up, the game will head into Overtime where the rules change to SUDDEN DEATH! The next player to score wins!

Now, Match Points haven't gone anywhere. In fact, they're still the default rule for most game types. However, an interesting change we've made is to how rules are applied.

With this update, each Game Mode (Classic, Hoop, etc.) has its own default ruleset! For example, Pin games default to 5 match points, rather than the default 10. Volley now defaults to a 3 minute Timed Match. And Hoop now uses the Bowling Ball by default!

Of course, you can change any of these yourself. Meaning Volley can be a Match Point game, Classic can be a Timed Match, etc. And you can tweak the other rules (like which pickups are allowed to spawn) just as before.

Speaking of which...

New Pickups
There are two new Pickups that come with 2nd Base. The first is Switchup. When your ball touches a Switchup coin, it will flip to the other team's possession!

Then, there's the Black Hole which works just like a portal to another dimension! When a ball touches this pickup, it will disappear for a moment before being teleported to a random position on the map! And stay frosty as the ball will maintain its momentum as it exits the Black Hole!
Steam Integration

For our Steam players, we've added new Steam integrations into this update! 2nd Base now supports Steam Rich Presence. There's also a button prompt to start an Online match using Remote Play Together. And we've even added Steam Achievements!

In order to add Steam Achievements, though, we also needed a way to track your stats. And that's why 2nd Base now incorporates a Stats panel on the Main Menu. (Note that this is available to all players, not just our Steam customers!)

This is all stored local to your device for maximum privacy. However, we have enabled Steam Cloud Saves which will back up your settings and your stats across devices!

Balancing & More
We've also taken the opportunity to balance the game, refine the controls, update the physics of the balls, and improve the player experience. (We've fixed a longstanding bug with popover menus closing their parent modal window.) And whole lot more! 

You can check out the absolutely MASSIVE changelog for the game here. And make sure you subscribe to our email newsletter where we do giveaways, show off behind the scenes stuff, and drop previews of our in-development work!

If you already own the game on Steam, you can just start playing. If you have the game on Itch you'll need to download the latest update. And if don't own the game yet, get it here on Steam!

notes.title: BETA 1.1.0 is now live
notes.content:
VERSION 1.1.0
Features
Added button prompt ("E" for keyboard, "Select" for gamepad) during team selection to start an online game through Remote Play TogetherAdded player statistics for Steam Achievements (only the first human player has their stats counted)Added the "Stats" menuPlayer stats were not collected previous to version 1.1 so all stats start at 0Added Steam AchievementsAdded Steam "Rich Presence"Added two new pickups"Switch Posession" - when the ball touches this pickup, it will change to the opposing team's possession"Black Hole" - when the ball touches this pickup, it will warp across the map!Added a birdAdded a "What's New" systemAdded a "What's New" sub menu that displays all the new, cool stuff in DudelingsAdded a "seen_whats_new_version_x_x_x" settingAdded a button to the "Main Menu" that players can use to see the new stuff

Improvements & Fixes
Improved the match rules menuUpdated controller detectionMoved Steam Notifications to the top right cornerImproved match setup workflow
First, choose your teamSelect the game typeSelect the mapOn this screen you may press "SELECT" (or "E" on your keyboard) to customize the match rulesMade the stars in the night sky twinkleFixed background animations on BeachAdded shader effect to BeachReduced chance that the sunset variant of Beach will be chosenUpdated benefactor's ad branding per their requestFixed issue where the button context bar was empty when first entering the Player Setup menu from the Main MenuImproved Pause Menu styling. Added toggle to show/hide Match Info using the "SELECT" (or "E" on your keyboard)Improved controller navigation in menus including focus change wrapping in the following menus:Main MenuSettings MenuVolume MenuPause Menu

Balance
Reduced chance the HARD and IMPOSSIBLE AIs will skip taking an action per AI think tickReduced bowling ball's weightRefactored balloon's statsLowered the balloon's weightIncreased frictionReduced all ball's mass scale when in the LARGE state

Known Issue
The game will randomly fail to launch when trying to initialize the Steam API. Relaunch the game once or twice and it should work. We're debugging this issue right now.

To join the beta, right-click on Dudelings from your library, then select Properties. On the Betas tab, use the "Beta Participation" drop down and choose "beta_1_1_0"

notes.title: Patch Notes v1.0.1
notes.content:
Gameplay

 Changed dashing to not cancel when button is released.
 Updated AI movements for Hard and Impossible difficulties.
 Updated Dudeling scroll movement to get canceled by other inputs.
 Added "punch missed" sound.


Menus and UI

 Updated How To Play menu.
 Fixed context bar flicker.
 Fixed context bar text spacing.
 Fixed issues with guessing controller type.
 Updated Player Options sub menu.
 Updated Splash Screen intro videos.
 Updated Main Menu video.
 Updated spacing for custom Dudelings font.
 Updated confirm message appearance.


General

 Updated scene switching speeds.
 Fixed controller vibration not always working.
